In figure $ABCDE$ shown above, which of the following are equal to the vector $\overset{\to }{BE}?$

I. $\overset{\to }{CB}+\overset{\to }{BA}+\overset{\to }{AE}$

II. $\overset{\to }{BC}-\overset{\to }{DC}+\overset{\to }{DE}$

III. $\overset{\to }{BA}+\overset{\to }{AE}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/2420154d44b786c6aad54212760e9a37ce67dbdce94a7043039f0e824c5ef9bc.png)

In parallelogram $ABCD$ shown above, which of the following equalities are true?

I. $\overrightarrow{CB}+\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CA}$

II. $\overrightarrow{CB}-\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{AC}$

III. $\overrightarrow{DC}=\overrightarrow{BA}$
current_example.worked_solution:
- Equality I is true. Indeed, $\overrightarrow{CB}+\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CA}.$

- Equality II is false. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CB}-\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{CB}+\overset{\to }{BA} \\  & =\overset{\to }{CA} \\  & \ne \overset{\to }{AC}\end{aligned}
$$

since $\overrightarrow{CA}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ have opposite directions.

- Equality III is false. Indeed, $\overrightarrow{DC}\neq\overrightarrow{BA}$ since they have opposite directions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
